== Switch Values ==
A "switch" statement in programming is just (in its simplest form) a fast, compact way to compare a single value to a large number of test cases. All the data is stored as return values for these switch statements.

The redundant naming scheme serves two purposes:
* Idiot proofing
* It allows simplification for caller function when passing values along the chain. I don't know how to explain it any better than that, but it is important that all the alias names are present. In short: it makes my life easier developing these templates.


<big>'''All test cases are lowercase!'''</big><br>
Another bit of idiot proofing is just making the request case-insensitive by converting it to lowercase before each comparison.

a. [[#minlevel-note-source|<span id="minlevel-note">&#94;</span> minlevel]]
<div class="class-style display-inline-block margin-left-10px" style="font-size:0.85em;"><!--
	-->Logic dictates that "minLevel" should always be 1. However, considering I ripped the data for many of these components directly from the game's code, it is hard to ignore the fact that some components' lower-level values and names are missing from the game's code entirely. Yet they still all still have icons.<br><!--
	-->It should be noted that the items in question are not currently available in-game and may be included in future releases.<!--
	-->Additionally, it could be an issue with my code not properly decrypting the unity code and extracting the data. But in at least one case, the game doesn't even have a reference to the component below level 3 (not even in the language files).<!--
--></div>

b. [[#maxlevel-note-source|<span id="maxlevel-note">&#94;</span> maxlevel]]
<div class="class-style display-inline-block margin-left-10px" style="font-size:0.85em;"><!--
	-->Should always be 7 unless future releases add higher level caps.<!--
--></div>

*Not all parameters are required for the template to function properly. However, the ability box will be incomplete without some parameters.

* <span style="color:red">REQUIRED</span> - Must be given a value
* <span style="color:orange">SEMI-REQUIRED</span> - Can be missing or have a null value, but it may have adverse effects. (usually has another parameter that takes over when the value is missing)
* <span style="color:blue">NOT-REQUIRED</span> - Can be missing or have a null value, but the ability box will be incomplete
* <span style="color:green">OPTIONAL</span> - Can be missing or have a null value with no repercussions.
